1	## Bet 5 — Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file
2	
3	### Goal
4	
5	A creator records a video podcast or an interview with two to four cameras and a microphone per
6	person. They line the files up with Synchronize Audio, select them, and choose Clip ▸ Switch by
7	Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking. It judges each microphone's speech against that
8	microphone's own level, so a guest's voice leaking into the host's microphone does not cut to
9	the host. It shows the wide shot while two people talk over each other, holds a minimum shot
10	length, and lets short replies ("yeah", "mm") pass without a cut. The result is one undo step:
11	a new Program track of ordinary clips, each a piece of one camera, over the cameras kept whole
12	and hidden on their own tracks. The microphones are not touched. Every cut can be rolled like
13	any other cut, and Clip ▸ Switch Angle re-picks the camera for one shot. Later phases add a
14	one-microphone mode that reads mouth movement with Vision, and an Angle Viewer that shows every
15	camera at once and switches while the timeline plays.
16	
17	Separately, Frame Job stops reading only the first audio track of a file. An OBS recording with
18	the mix on track 1, the microphone on track 2 and the desktop on track 3 imports all three. A
19	recorder or mixer file with many channels in one track (a RØDECaster Pro II, a Zoom F-series,
20	a MixPre) offers each channel as its own source, and so does a wireless kit that records two
21	people on the left and right of one stereo track. Each track or channel can be placed as its own
22	clip with its own audio chain, and Detach Audio makes one linked sound clip per track. Every
23	measurement — the waveform, loudness, Normalize, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech, Remove Silences,
24	Synchronize Audio, transcription — reads the track or channel the clip plays.
25	
26	Every command has its MCP tool. No phase needs a key.
27	
28	### Owner's answers applied
29	
30	- **All six bets are in one road map.** This is bet 5, prefix SW; its phases are SW1–SW9b.
31	- **Every spec §1 non-goal is lifted.** For this bet that means multicam. The bet builds
32	  multicam in full: synced angles, a program track of shots, re-picking, an Angle Viewer and
33	  switching while playing (SW1, SW2, SW9a, SW9b). It does this without a multicam source kind:
34	  the shots are ordinary clips on an ordinary track (SW-10, SW-90). That is a design choice, not
35	  a non-goal; the owner can ask for a multicam clip instead at SW9a.
36	- **§11 decisions that implement a non-goal stand until a phase amends them in writing.** This
37	  bet amends none of them. Nest clips keep having no in point (`core/src/nest.rs:22`), there is
38	  still one kind of track (spec §2), and the effect vocabulary stays closed (R5-1).
39	- **Input Monitoring.** Not used by this bet.
40	- **The key rule.** Nothing in this bet uses a language model or a cloud model. Switch by
41	  Speaker reads the loudness cache, Silero VAD's speech cache and, in SW8, Vision face
42	  landmarks — all on the device, none needing a key. The Assistant can call the bet's tools on
43	  its own key, as it calls every tool. Transcribing a second audio track with AssemblyAI needs
44	  the AssemblyAI key exactly as transcribing the first does today.
45	- **Lead segments.** Video podcasts are the third segment, so the switch (SW1, SW2) is
46	  scheduled after the first phases of bets 1–4. Reading every audio track (SW3, SW4, SW5) also
47	  serves the first segment: screen recordists who record with OBS keep their microphone on its
48	  own track. The orchestrator's default lets those three phases start early, in a lane of their
49	  own.
50	- **Real use.** The owner cuts one real video per lead segment alongside bet 1. For podcasts,
51	  JOB-51 asks the owner to cut one real episode with Switch by Speaker once SW2 lands; the
52	  verdict is recorded as SW-29, the way GR-9 recorded grading's trial.
53	- **Build arrangement.** Every format number below is provisional ("format 38p") until its
54	  phase lands; the integrator renumbers on collision. Decision IDs are SW-n0…SW-n9 per phase;
55	  scope-level drafts are offered to CJ0 for numbering.
56	
57	### How it fits the tree
58	
59	At `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.
60	
61	**A media is one file with one sound.**
62	- `Media` (`core/src/model.rs:162–192`, the file 570 lines) records `has_audio: bool` and
63	  nothing about how many audio tracks or channels the file has. Its `speech` spans
64	  (format 29, AU-110) belong to the file as a whole.
65	- `add_media` treats a path already in the list as an identity (`core/src/edit_track.rs:476`,
66	  the doc above it: "two entries for one path would each carry their own bookmark, thumbnails
67	  and peaks"). A second audio track therefore cannot be a second media row; it must be
68	  something a CLIP chooses.
69	- `Source::Media` is `{media, in, reversed}` (`core/src/model.rs:292–315`). `reversed` is the
70	  precedent for a fact about what a clip reads that changes neither the plan's structure nor
71	  the recipe.
72	
73	**Every reader takes the first audio track.**
74	- The probe counts audio tracks and keeps only whether there is one
75	  (`app/Sources/MediaImporter.swift:79`, `hasAudio: !audioTracks.isEmpty` at :114).
76	- The builder's one synchronous track lookup answers `.first`
77	  (`app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift:423`, 546 lines), reached through `assetTrack`
78	  (:400–412) from `resolveSource` (`CompositionBuilder+AudioTracks.swift:64`) and from the
79	  48 kHz copy (`AudioRateCopy.swift:320–345`).
80	- Direct callers of `firstTrack(of:mediaType: .audio)`: `Transcriber+Extract.swift:106`,
81	  `VoiceRenderer.swift:66`, `RampAudioRenderer.swift:116`, `IsolationRenderer.swift:109`,
82	  `ReverseRenderer.swift:201` (574 lines), `RampAudioCache.swift:136` and `:191`.
83	  `CompositionBuilder+Silence.swift:49` reads the bundled `Silence.caf` and is unaffected.
84	- The four cache passes take `loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio)?.first`:
85	  peaks `MediaImporter.swift:478`, loudness :506, sync features :537, speech :581.
86	- The 48 kHz copy is keyed by the file alone (`AudioRateCopy.swift:56–70`, "path|size|mtime|v")
87	  and substituted per media id (`:320–345`), so two streams of one 44.1 kHz file would collide.
88	- The reversed copy is one movie per media, `cache/reversed/<media>-<digest>.mov`
89	  (`ReverseCache.swift:64–65`), carrying the first audio track.
90	- Readers that do NOT need changing: everything that reads the built composition's tracks —
91	  `ScrubGrains.swift:75`, `ExportMixRead.swift:50`, `ExporterWriter+Audio.swift:42`,
92	  `ExporterWriter+Settings.swift:69`, `ExporterWriter.swift:141`, `ProcessedLoudness.swift:210`,
93	  `ExporterLoudness.swift:109`, `ExportWebMWriter.swift:108`.
94	
95	**Matroska and ffmpeg also take the first audio stream.**
96	- `core/src/container.rs` (358 lines; new-module cap 400) indexes "its first video track and its
97	  first audio track" (:1–5, :90–94); `rc_container_sample`'s track argument is `VIDEO = 0`,
98	  `AUDIO = 1` (:34–37). `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift` (539) copies those two. #216-R records it.
99	  OBS records Matroska by default.
100	- The opt-in ffmpeg step maps `-map 0:a:0?` (`FFmpegRewrap+Plan.swift:233`).
101	
102	**The caches are per media id.**
103	- `cache/peaks/<id>.bin`, `cache/speech/<id>.bin` (`MediaCacheFiles.swift:101–118`, 452 lines),
104	  `cache/loudness/<id>.bin` (AU-10), `cache/sync/<id>.bin` and `.pcm` (SY-11),
105	  `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` (R6-3), `cache/device-transcripts/<id>-<lang>.json`
106	  (`DeviceTranscriptCache.swift:102`).
107	- `MediaCacheLoader` memoises by `UInt32` media id (`MediaPeaks.swift:226`); `ClipLoudness`,
108	  `MediaSpeech`, `DuckSpeech`, `AudioDynamicsLevels`, `SilenceDetector` and `AudioSync`
109	  (`AudioSync.swift:240–273`, features, samples and speech by media) all read through media ids.
110	- The loudness cache stores stereo as `zL, zR, zLR` per 10 ms (AU-10), so a left or right
111	  pick's level is already measurable (AU-35's matrix). A file of more than two channels is read
112	  again as two. The speech cache is one mono mixdown on Silero's 32 ms grid (silence.md), so a
113	  stereo file with one person per side has no per-person speech today.
114	- silence.md: "The probabilities are a per-media CACHE, never computed at feature time." The
115	  switch obeys it: it reads caches and does arithmetic.
116	
117	**Channels.** `audio.channels` (AU-34: both, left, right, swapped) is a pick at the head of the
118	tap. The tap accepts any channel count (`AudioTap.swift:141–170`, 507 lines). What AVFoundation
119	hands the tap, and what the export's mix does, for a stream of more than two channels has never
120	been measured (SW-S1).
121	
122	**Links are pairs.** `Clip.linked` names one partner, mutually (`core/src/edit_link.rs`, 335;
123	AU-90…AU-97). Picture plus three sound tracks cannot be one linked set today.
124	
125	**What the switch can build on.**
126	- Synchronize Audio's shape: `read` takes everything off the document once, `plan` is pure and
127	  answers ops or every reason it refuses (`AudioSync.swift:1–60`, 551 lines). The switch copies
128	  that shape.
129	- A hidden track's clips are not decoded: video is placed only when `instance.shows_video()`
130	  (`core/src/evaluate.rs:451`; `nest.rs:140`), and sound is placed when `plays_audio()`, which
131	  reads only `enabled.audio` (`nest.rs:153`). A hidden angle track costs no decode and still
132	  sounds.
133	- The plan's A/B assignment puts a timeline track's adjacent clips on one composition track
134	  (`evaluate.rs:433`); the decoder budget warns past eight video composition tracks
135	  (`plan.rs:19`). A program track of alternating cameras is therefore one composition track
136	  whose source changes at each cut (SW-S2 (a)).
137	- `MAX_CLIPS` is 4,096, nested clips included (`core/src/format.rs:27`, `check_caps` :57).
138	- No existing op copies a piece of a clip to another track at the same time: `duplicate`
139	  places a copy one selection-span later; `add_blurred_background` copies a whole clip to a new

141	  one way a source in point moves". SW1 adds the op.

144	- Nest clips have no in point (`nest.rs:22`): a split nest replays from its top. A multicam clip

146	- `play_preview` (dev tool, G-36) answers the frames a window's preview composed; it is the
147	  instrument for SW-S2.
148	
149	**Sizes that set tolls.** `ProjectSnapshot.swift` 1,454 (over; `ClipSource` :901, `ClipSnapshot`

151	`AudioPane.swift` 554; `ReverseRenderer.swift` 574; `Playback.swift` 592; `AudioSync.swift` 551;

154	`core/src/container.rs` 358 of 400. `AgentServer.swift`, `EditorViewController.swift` and

156	65 times in 39 Swift files, most of them `ClipSource.media` patterns, so a new stream or channel

159	A hidden clip is not placed in either branch of the assignment (`evaluate.rs:451` for a ramped

161	
162	### Decisions to record or amend
163	
164	Drafts, in the style of `designs/spec/11-decisions/`. Each is recorded in
165	`designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` before its phase's code.
166	
167	**Scope (offered to CJ0 for numbering).**
168	- **CJ-? (SW scope) — Multicam is in, as a program track over angle tracks.** Synced camera
169	  clips (angles) stay whole on their own tracks; a program track holds the shots, each an
170	  ordinary clip copied from an angle at the same time. Switch by Speaker writes the program
171	  track, Switch Angle re-picks a shot, and the Angle Viewer shows every angle and switches while
172	  playing. There is no multicam source kind and no nest in point: every shot can be rolled,
173	  trimmed, graded and deleted like any clip, and spec §2's one kind of track holds. Draft text
174	  for spec §1: "Multicam is in (CJ-?, SW-10, SW-90): synced angles stay whole on their own
175	  tracks and a program track holds the shots, each an ordinary clip; there is no multicam
176	  clip."
177	
178	**SW1 — the piece copy and Switch Angle.**
179	- **SW-10 — The switch writes a program track; it does not cut the cameras in place.** The
180	  orchestrator's first reading was picture-only cuts on the stacked camera tracks (`split` every
181	  camera at every cut, `set_enabled {video: false}` on the pieces not shown). Rejected: it makes
182	  two to three clips per shot where the program track makes one (a four-camera, three-hour show
183	  at 8 s shots is about 5,400 against about 1,350 — the stacked form passes `MAX_CLIPS`); moving
184	  one cut means trimming pieces on two or three tracks, where on the program track it is an
185	  ordinary roll; and re-picking means splitting a disabled piece first. Both forms decode one
186	  camera at a time, since hidden and disabled pictures are not placed (`evaluate.rs:451`).
187	- **SW-11 — `copy_pieces {clip, track, ranges, video?, audio?}`.** Copies the pieces of `clip`
188	  between each range's ends onto `track` at the same times, with fresh ids. `ranges` is a list
189	  of `[from, to]` project times; each end is snapped as `split` snaps its `at`; the ranges are
190	  sorted, must not overlap one another and must lie inside the clip. `video` and `audio`, when
191	  given, set each piece's `enabled` switches; absent, a piece keeps the clip's. Refused, each in
192	  its own sentence: a nest clip ("clip N is a nest: a piece of it would replay the nest from its
193	  first frame"); a range outside the clip; overlapping ranges; a locked destination; a
194	  destination holding a clip over a range ("track T holds clip C between A and B"). `Err` for
195	  an unknown clip or track. An empty `ranges` is an identity. A copy has no transition, and its
196	  `linked` (or, after SW7a, its `link`) is cleared. Allowed inside a nest through `scope`.
197	- **SW-12 — A piece is exactly the middle a `split` at its two ends would leave.** Its source
198	  window, a ramp's map and rate (SR-18), its actions clipped to it, a graphic's `in` and
199	  `length` (G-9) and its words rebased (W-3) all come from `split`'s own arithmetic, called on a
200	  scratch copy; `copy_pieces` has no source arithmetic of its own. A piece of a synced, drift-
201	  corrected angle (SY-8's `set_speed`) therefore plays the angle's frames at the angle's times.
202	- **SW-13 — Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ re-picks one shot.** The submenu lists, for the one selected
203	  clip, every other media clip with pictures in the same container whose span covers the
204	  selected clip's whole span, front track first, named by clip name else media name, up to
205	  nine. Choosing one deletes the shot and `copy_pieces` the angle over the same span onto the
206	  same track with the shot's `enabled` switches, as one undo step "Switch Angle". The tool
207	  `switch_angle {clip, angle}` does the same and refuses an angle that does not cover the shot.
208	- **SW-14 — A re-picked shot keeps its span, its switches and its transition, and nothing
209	  else.** The new piece is the angle's own: a punch-in scale, a grade or an action the old shot
210	  carried does not carry over, and the guide says so. Its transition is put back with
211	  `add_transition` at the old kind and duration when the angle's handles allow it, else dropped
212	  and the step's name says "Switch Angle (transition removed)".
213	
214	**SW2 — Switch by Speaker.**
215	- **SW-20 — The inputs.** Angles are the selected clips with pictures (two to nine). Speakers
216	  are pairs of a microphone and an angle: a microphone is a selected clip that plays sound, and
217	  its angle is the camera showing that person — any angle, the wide included. The default
218	  pairing: a microphone that is itself an angle (a lavalier into the camera) pairs with itself;
219	  the others pair, in track order front to back, with the remaining angles in track order. The
220	  wide is optional and is the angle no microphone names, when exactly one is left. The range is
221	  the In/Out range when set, else the span every angle covers. A microphone's steps outside its
222	  own clip count as silent. The switch trusts the placement; it does not check sync, and the
223	  guide says to run Synchronize Audio first.
224	- **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms timeline grid over
225	  the range, for each microphone m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's
226	  K-weighted mean square, through the clip's own channel matrix (AU-35) and source map,
227	  averaged over 100 ms; its voice v_m(k) is the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk

840	- **Acceptance.** The viewer's live cells follow SW-S2 (c) and stay in step with the program.
841	- **Proof** (`tools/proof/angle_viewer_proof.py`, Release). V1 each live cell delivers ≥ 98 % of
842	  due frames over 60 s. V2 `play_preview` of the program with the viewer open stays within SW-S2's
843	  band. V3 a cell's pixels at a paused time match `render_frame` of that angle alone, scaled. V4 a
844	  click switches from the playhead, one undo step.
845	- **Mutants** (3). Hidden angles left out of the plan (V1); a cell offset by one frame (V3); the
846	  click switching the whole shot (V4).
847	- **Manual checks.** **JOB-56 — The viewer's feel.** Do: play a four-angle episode with the
848	  viewer open. Expect: the cells move with the program, and the outline follows the cuts.
849	- **Depends on.** SW2, SW-S2 (re-run on the owner's files first).
850	- **Questions for the owner at phase time.** (1) Angles derived (SW-90) or stored on the program
851	  track (`tracks[].angles`, a format bump and a toll moving `TrackSnapshot` out of
852	  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`)? Recommended: derived. (2) A panel beside the preview (recommended,
853	  like Scopes) or a window? (3) A multicam clip with angles inside one clip instead of a program
854	  track? Recommended: no (CJ-? scope draft).
855	
856	#### SW9b — Switching while playing
857	
858	- **What a person gets.** With the viewer shown, 1–9 or a click while playing cut to that angle at
859	  that moment; the marks show on the program track, and stopping applies them as one undo step.
860	- **Core.** None (`split`, `delete`, `copy_pieces` grouped).
861	- **FFI.** None.
862	- **Swift.** `EditorViewController+AngleSwitch.swift` (new: the recorder of presses and its
863	  apply); the bare-digit arms in `handleEditorCharacter` (wiring only in the frozen file);
864	  `TimelineView+AnglePresses.swift` (new: the pending marks); `EditorWindow`'s Space routing
865	  unchanged.
866	- **MCP.** `switch_angles {track, cuts: [{at, angle}]}` (SW-96).
867	- **Docs.** Spec §9 (keys 1–9), §7.9a; `docs/guide/multicam.md`, `menus-and-shortcuts.md`.
868	- **Acceptance.** Presses land on their frame-snapped times as one step; nothing rebuilds while
869	  playing.
870	- **Proof.** A probe of the press recorder (replacement within a frame, the hold to the next cut);
871	  MCP rows: W1 `switch_angles` with five cuts gives five shots and one undo step, W2 the build
872	  count does not change while presses are recorded (the dev tool counts rebuilds).
873	- **Mutants** (2). A press applied at once rather than at stop (W2); a press within a frame kept
874	  as a second cut (probe).
875	- **Manual checks.** **JOB-57 — Switching while playing.** Do: play an episode and press 1 and 2
876	  as the speakers change. Expect: playback never stutters at a press, and the cuts land where
877	  pressed.
878	- **Depends on.** SW9a.
879	- **Questions for the owner at phase time.** (1) Apply at stop (recommended) or edit live?
880	
881	### Samples and fixtures
882	
883	**From the owner** (the GH5 and the iPhone 18 Pro; each row goes into `samples/README.md` with
884	what it measures):
885	- **S-POD-2CAM** — ten to fifteen minutes of two people talking: the GH5 on one person, the
886	  iPhone on the other, both 4K, each person on their own microphone (two separate recorder files,
887	  or two OBS tracks), a clap at the start; turn-taking, short replies, laughter and some talking
888	  over. A third angle (a wide from a second phone or the Mac's camera through Frame Job's
889	  recorder) if possible. Measures SW-S4, SW2's JOB-51, SW-S2 on real codecs, SW-S3's ground
890	  truth.
891	- **S-POD-SPLIT** — the same kind of conversation on a wireless kit recording both people into
892	  one camera's stereo track (left and right), if the owner has one. Measures SW6.
893	- **S-POD-1MIC** — the same conversation with one microphone between the two people and the two
894	  cameras. Measures SW-S3 and SW8.
895	- **S-OBS** — an OBS recording of the screen with the mix on track 1, a microphone on track 2
896	  and the desktop on track 3, once as `.mkv` and once as Hybrid MP4. Measures SW3 and SW5.
897	- **S-IPHONE-SPATIAL** — a short iPhone 18 Pro clip with Spatial Audio on. Measures SW-S1 (f):
898	  how many audio tracks the phone writes and whether each decodes.
899	- **S-RECORDER** — a multitrack file from a recorder or mixer (RØDECaster Pro II, Zoom F-series
900	  or H-series in multitrack mode, a MixPre), if the owner has one. Measures SW6.
901	
902	**Synthetic, made by the proofs** (ffmpeg and macOS `say`; no proof waits for a sample):
903	- **F-TURNS** — two macOS voices reading a scripted turn table (turns, short replies under 1 s,
904	  stretches of talking over, pauses); each microphone is its voice at 0 dB, the other at a set
905	  bleed (−12, −18, −24 dB) and pink noise (−55, −45 dBFS); three 1080p colour-card "cameras"
906	  (one per person and a wide) with burned-in frame counters. The table is the truth (SW-27).
907	- **F-MULTITRACK** — MOV, MP4 and MKV files with video and three audio tracks (distinct tones,
908	  and distinct speech placements for SW4), one at 44.1 kHz.
909	- **F-POLY** — a 6-channel 48 kHz 24-bit WAV, a tone or a voice per channel, with and without a
910	  channel layout; and a 6-channel AAC.
911	- **F-SPLIT** — a stereo file with one voice per side and bleed between them.
912	- **F-4K** — ten-minute 3840×2160 sources at 29.97 and 59.94 fps in H.264 at 100 Mb/s, HEVC
913	  Main 10 and ProRes 422 HQ, with noise so the encoders work (VideoToolbox encoders through
914	  ffmpeg), for SW-S2.
915	
916	### Risks
917	
918	- **AVFoundation and many channels.** What the tap and the export's mix see for a stream of more
919	  than two channels is unmeasured; SW-S1 decides between the tap and a copy, and the copy costs
920	  temporary disk (about 0.5 GB an hour per channel at 24-bit mono) and render time.
921	- **Cuts between long-GOP 4K files on one composition track may hitch.** SW-S2 (a) measures it;
922	  the fix is a plan change.
923	- **Rebuild time with a thousand shots** is unmeasured (SW-S2 (b)); the owner's order puts
924	  performance work after features, so a shortfall becomes a recorded limit and an issue.
925	- **Bleed and loud laughter.** One margin will not suit every room; SW-S4 sets the defaults and
926	  the sheet exposes the margin.
927	- **Sync.** The switch trusts the placement. A slipped or moved shot falls out of sync with the
928	  microphones like any synced clip; the guide says so.
929	- **`MAX_CLIPS`.** A three-hour show at a two-second minimum can pass 4,096; the switch refuses
930	  first and says what to raise.
931	- **Hidden angles still sound.** Camera scratch audio doubles the microphones unless muted; the
932	  switch mutes non-microphone angles by default.
933	- **Cache volume.** Per-source caches multiply the sync features (23 MB an hour each) and speech
934	  files; SW-41 makes only the sources clips play.
935	- **Link groups change a format-28 field and every link rule.** AP9's proof re-runs whole; one
936	  mutant per rule.
937	- **Stream order.** If AVFoundation's order differs from the container's (SW-S1 (a)), track names
938	  in other apps will not match Frame Job's numbers.
939	- **iPhone Spatial Audio** may add tracks AVFoundation cannot decode on this Mac; they are left
940	  out (SW-30), and track 1 stays what every build has played.
941	- **Mouth activity** fails on profiles, small faces in wide shots, beards and hands over mouths;
942	  SW-S3 gates SW8.
943	- **Four live 4K decodes** may exceed the Mac's decoders; SW-S2 (c) sets the viewer's live cells.
944	- **Shared files.** `op_table.rs` (374 of 400), `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` (554) and
945	  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (1,454) take rows from every bet; the tolls land in CJ0.
946	
947	### Not in this bet
948	
949	Lifted non-goals that this bet does not build, and why, each to be filed as a candidate issue
950	when the road map closes:
951	- **A multicam source kind** (one clip holding every angle, as Final Cut Pro's): the program
952	  track does the same jobs with ordinary clips (SW-10, SW-90).
953	- **Proxies:** only if SW-S2 shows a shortfall, as a Performance-project issue.
954	- **Virtual angles from one wide camera** (cropping to each face): bet 3's subject tracking can
955	  supply the framing; a candidate after VR.
956	- **Laughter to the wide shot:** needs Find Clips' Sound Analysis cache; a candidate after FC.
957	- **Telling speakers apart by voice on one microphone with no faces** (diarization): Apple's
958	  frameworks have no on-device diarization; AssemblyAI's speaker labels would make it a
959	  key-gated cloud feature. A candidate, keyed if built.
960	- **Layouts during crosstalk** (side by side): bet 6's layouts can supply them; a candidate.
961	- **Exporting the multicam edit to another editor** (FCPXML, AAF): a candidate.
962	- **Live multi-camera capture and remote guests:** the survey's "not worth chasing"; no longer a
963	  non-goal, but not built here.
964	- **A multitrack movie as an export:** AU-101 chose separate stem files, and that stands.
965

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four

  deliberate overrides of model values (the other: a matte layer's `blend`,

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers

  `MAX_STORED_TICKS`: ±9,000,000,000,000,000 for stored media, markers,
  clips, source positions and actions, including clip/action endpoints in
  i128. `Project::validate` and `format::write` both call it; vocabulary
  property timings and finite positive speeds are outside this envelope.
- `outcome.rs` — `Outcome`, the THREE arms every edit answers with
  (spec §5.5): applied with the new project, an identity, or refused with
  the rule's own sentence. An enum and its doc, nothing else. It is an enum
  rather than a side channel so that a site which has not decided which
  answer it gives does not compile; the fourth possibility, a request that
  could not be read, stays the `Err(String)` beside it. Its `Identity` doc
  is also the one place that says which non-edits speak and which stay
  identities on purpose (spec §5.5, §11 #88).
- `edit.rs` — the op enum, `parse` and `apply`. **Its module doc IS the op
  table's SEMANTICS half** — what each op means, and what an absent
  optional argument means — where `op_table.rs` is the ARGUMENTS half;
  `app/Sources/ReelOps.swift`'s typed builders, `AgentCatalog*.swift`'s
  tools and spec §6 mirror the two together. `OP_NAMES` is re-exported from
  here, at the path it has always had. `parse` answers an `Envelope` — the
  op AND the envelope's `scope` — and `apply_op(&Op)` knows nothing about
  nests. The semantics table is the reason this file is over the size cap
  and stays exempt (below).
- `op_table.rs` — the op table as DATA (road map 7's D3): one `OpRow` per
  op and one `Argument` per argument — its name, its `Kind` (`Kind::Output`
  for `set_canvas`'s dynamic range, `Kind::Blending` for its blending),
  whether the
  decoder requires it and, for the few that have one, its `Bound` — and
  `OP_NAMES` as a projection of it, re-exported by
  `edit.rs` so no caller moved. A published interface, where the `Op` enum
  and the dispatch are its implementation. Its one reader in the crate is
  `op_schema.rs`, which carries the rows out through the FFI; the APP's
  reader is every one of the sixty-four op tools in the agent catalog,
  which print these rows instead of restating them. **A `Bound` is
  published only where the core REFUSES outside it** — `set_canvas`'s two
  dimensions, sourced from `edit_canvas.rs`'s own constants, and
  `add_graphic_clip`'s `width` and `height`, from `model_graphic.rs`'s, never
  retyped — and never where it CLAMPS, which is the app's to say in its
  prose. A row holds no prose, no semantics and no default spelled twice;
  `Kind` is closed (twenty-three kinds; `Texts`, a list of strings, is
  `set_action_end`'s `off`), carries each vocabulary's members, and has exactly ONE
  kind per answer serde gives, because a distinction the
  decoder cannot see is one no test could prove. Nothing here is the
  authority — the enum's fields are, and `core/tests/op_table.rs` proves
  every row by asking the decoder. Capped at 400 lines like any new module:
  it does NOT inherit `edit.rs`'s table exemption.
- `op_schema.rs` — `op_table.rs` written as JSON Schema, which is what
  `rc_op_schemas` publishes (road map 7's D3·2): one object per op, its
  properties the arguments and its `required` the ones the decoder will not
  do without. **The match over `Kind` is exhaustive** — a kind added to the
  table does not compile until this says what JSON it is — and it is a
  module of its own because a row changes when an OP does and this changes
  when the published DIALECT does. It says nothing about what an argument is
  FOR (the catalog's prose), nothing about what a patch may CARRY
  (`Kind::Object` is an object with no properties; D1 left the core the one
  validator of that), and nothing about `additionalProperties` on an op,
  because the catalog merges `project` and `scope` in afterwards. Tested
  through the FFI in `core/tests/op_schemas.rs`.

  VIEW project from the nest (its tracks and clips at top level, its frozen
  size as the canvas, the parent's rate, media, `next_id` and nests, no
  markers), applies the op to it UNCHANGED, merges back. So `Project::clip`
  keeps its one meaning and no op has a nest-aware branch. Three things are
  counter-intuitive and measured: the scoped nest's own row stays in the view
  with its tracks and clips EMPTIED (removing it dangles every other nest's
  reference; leaving it whole doubles every id under `validate`); the nests
  write-back is union first, orphans after; and **a scoped apply has a wider
  `Err` arm than any unscoped op** — `check_caps` and `check_nesting` are
  document-wide and run on the MERGED parent, so an op valid inside the nest
  can still return `Err`. `refused_inside` is an EXHAUSTIVE match over every
  op, so a new op does not compile until it is classified. The READ half is
  `rc_project_scoped` in `ffi.rs`, which calls the same `scoped_view`.

- `edit_fit.rs` — `fit_scale` and `fill_scale` (Fit is a RESCUE for oversized

  from `vpcc`; spec §11 CX-16 (10)); the app writes the blobs and the PQ label only for transfer 16. The only payload read
  is the first VP9 keyframe's header, each Opus packet's TOC and each Vorbis
  packet's first byte.
- `ffi_graphic.rs` — the twelve `rc_graphic_*` exports (road map 10 §5e; the
  eleventh `rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39: set the decoded-image cache's
  limit, answer its bytes; the twelfth `rc_graphic_library_usage`, G-46: the
  font files and assets the library's draws used; two re-exported from
  `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`)
  and the ONLY module of `core/src/` that names the `graphic` crate (spec
  §11 G-2; `core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` reads `core/src/` to hold it). An
  `RcGraphicLibrary` is a BUILDER that the first compile or rasterize
  FREEZES into one `Arc<graphic::Library>` (the crate's `Library` is
  immutable — its `version` hashes every byte); an add after that is
  refused. `RcGraphic` wraps `graphic::Module`, whose `Arc` keeps the
  fonts alive past the library's free. `diag_out` is a JSON array of
  Diagnostics, exactly one error on failure; its panic arm goes through
  `ffi_util.rs`'s `fallible_op_wrapped`. `rc_graphic_library_families`
  answers the frozen library's family names as JSON — the engine's own,
  which a `font-family` must match (CoreText names 13 of 2500 host fonts
  differently) — and freezes it. `rc_graphic_describe` answers `{meta,
  schema, revision, warnings}`, `warnings` being `Module::warnings()`
  through `Diagnostic::to_json` (spec §11 G-24 (a)). G6 phase 5's toll T1
  moved the crate-free builder half to `ffi_graphic_pending.rs`
  (core-file-history); what is left names the crate (`diag_json`/
  `diag_error` name `Diagnostic`). `ffi_util.rs` holds the two crate-free helpers it gave up:
  `read_bytes` (a pointer and a length into an owned `Vec`, `bytes is NULL`
  refused) and `free_boxed` (drops a handle `boxed` made, under
  `fallible_op` with no channel; NULL a no-op).
- `ffi_graphic_pending.rs` — the library builder's crate-free half (G6
  phase 5's toll T1): `FROZEN`, `Pending`, `lock`, `rc_graphic_library_new`
  and `rc_graphic_library_add_asset`, `pub(crate)` for `ffi_graphic.rs`;
  it names no `graphic` item (G-2).

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit_clip.rs` and `edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/core/CLAUDE.md:

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs`, re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —
  no module of the model may name the crate, G-2; a non-boolean `animate`
  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`
  is a removal and is never checked), `check_typed` (one value against its
  entry, answered normalised; `edit_action_graphic.rs` calls it under
  `graphic.props.<key>`), `check_count` (on the map about to be
  STORED). **A props map is changed only by `insert` and
  `shift_remove`**: under `preserve_order`, `Map::remove` is `swap_remove`,
  and `Project ==` cannot see the reorder.
- `model_look.rs` — the look vocabulary (spec §11 GR-7): `Look {kind, amount}`
  (the FIELD `VideoProps.look`, optional, written only when set) and the eight
  built-in looks' definitions as data — Color's four, Light's nine and a split
  tone each — which the recipe's `look` key carries whole, so retuning a look
  is a core change only. `actions.rs` turns a merged look with no valid `kind`
  into `null`, so an action's end can never drop the clip's video group.
  `kind: "lut"` names an imported LUT's media (`media`); `BUILT_IN` is the
  eight. `actions.rs`'s object discriminants (`kind`, `media`) switch at an
  action's end instead of interpolating.
- `model_grade.rs` — tier 2's grading vocabulary (format 16, spec §11 GR-11): `Wheels {lift,
  gamma, gain}`, each a `Wheel {x, y, master}`, the FIELD `VideoProps.wheels` written only when
  not neutral and each key only when not 0; `actions::wheels_json` writes all nine for the
  evaluator, the patch template and the recipe, as `color_json` does tone's. Format 17 (GR-12)
  adds `Curves {master, red, green, blue}`, each an optional list of 2–16 `[x, y]` points
  (`CurvePoint`), the FIELD `VideoProps.curves` written only when not the identity
  (`curve_is_identity`: every y = x, from x 0 to x 1); format 20 (GR-32) adds `hue_hue` and
  `hue_sat` (`[hue, value]` points, 0 ≤ hue < 360) and `CurveDomain` (each channel's identity,
  neutral and value range; `named()` and `named_mut()` give each channel's), a hue curve the
  identity when every value is its neutral; `actions_curves.rs`'s `curves_json` writes all
  six, an absent one as its domain's identity. Format 18 (GR-13) adds `Qualifier {hue,
  saturation, luma, invert}` (`HueRange {center, width, softness}` in degrees, `LevelRange
  {low, high, softness}` 0–1, a range `None` when off), the FIELD `VideoProps.qualifier`,
  written only when not neutral; it acts only on an adjustment clip. Format 21 (GR-35)
  adds `Qualifier.blur` (0…1, written only when above 0, after `invert`) and
  `QUALIFIER_BLUR_MAX`; `is_neutral` counts it, so a blur alone is kept. Re-exported whole
  by `model_props.rs`.
- `cube.rs` — the `.cube` reader (spec §11 GR-8): 3D only, size 2–65, the
  default domain; anything else refused by line and name. `ffi_cube.rs` — the
  four `rc_cube_*` exports. `lut.rs` — a LUT media's rules: placing one is
  refused, removing one clears the looks that name it (the clips stay) and
  the Camera Log of the media it converts, refusing first without
  `with_clips`; paste carries it by path. `Project::check_lut_reference` is
  the one check of a LUT named by media id, keyed by its field
  (`video.look.media`, `color.lut`).
- `model_media_color.rs` — camera log's vocabulary (format version 19,
  spec §11 GR-16): `LogCurve`, `CameraGamut` (`LogCurve::gamuts`, its
  default first) and `MediaColor` (`log`, `gamut`, `lut`, `detected`, and
  since format 22 `pq`, a `PqColor` — import's `file` reading, its
  `PeakSource`, the override `peak`, `PEAK_MIN`..`PEAK_MAX` — each written
  only when set; format 25 adds `canon_log2`, `canon_log3` and the gamut
  `cinema_gamut`, each Canon curve pairing with Cinema Gamut (its default)
  or BT.2020, spec §11 HD-17), re-exported by `model.rs` for `Media.color`.
  `media_color.rs` — its rules: `set_media_color` (a strict reader,
  `detected` and `pq` refused, its `peak` the override, "needs log or lut"
  judged on what the caller asked for, spec §11 HD-12),
  `check_media_color` (each refusal its own sentence; `add_media` and
  `validate` call it too; a `pq`-only colour stands), `without_camera_log`
  (what a LUT's removal or a paste leaves: the reading), `media_input` (the
  recipe layer's and the plan segment's `input`, with the effective `peak`)
  and `media_converted_by`.
- `dynamic_range.rs` — an HLG project's deliverables (spec §11 HD-5,
  HD-14): `DynamicRange` (`hlg`, `pq`, `sdr`), spelled `dynamic_range` both
  as an export override and as a recipe option; `deliverable` answers `None`
  for an audio row and for every row of an SDR project, else the picture:
  the six HDR rows (`hevc_10bit`, `av1`, `av1_webm`, `vp9_webm`, `prores_422`, `prores_4444`) carry
  `hlg` (the default), `pq` or `sdr`, every other video row writes the SDR
  version, and `hlg`/`pq` are refused in an SDR project and on any other row, each in its own sentence.
- `av1_mp4.rs` · `ffi_av1.rs` — AV1 in MP4 (spec §11 CX-12, road map
  codec-export C1): `av1C` built from a full parse of the sequence header OBU,
  temporal delimiters stripped in place, and the `av01` brand put into `ftyp`
  (no `mp41` to replace is an error, never a file without `av01`); the three
  `rc_av1_*` exports. `leb128` is shared with `hdr10.rs`. The export table's
  `writer` field (`svt_av1` on `av1` and `av1_webm`; `avf_preset` stays the ImageIO
  switch) and the `encoder_speed` override (`faster` | `balanced` | `smaller`,
  refused on any other row) are `export_table.rs`' and `export_overrides.rs`';
  `Container` is `export_container.rs`'.
- `export_encoder.rs` — the bundled encoders' route and speeds (spec §11
  CX-12, CX-16): `Writer` (`svt_av1`, `libvpx`; none is AVFoundation; `takes_speed`
  false for libvpx's one speed) and `EncoderSpeed`, moved whole out of
  `export_table.rs` (codec-export C3's toll, a pure move) and re-exported there.

- `speed_segments.rs` — the map cut into plan pieces: `Held` at one rate

- `edit_action_speed.rs` — `set_action_end`'s speed arm and the overrun

  `largest_fitting_end_rate`, which split's eased tail also uses, over the

- `edit_action_ramp.rs` — `add_speed_ramp`, the ramp presets (SR-23, #340):

- `edit_action_graphic.rs` — `set_action_end`'s graphic arm (G-34):

- `edit_paste_attributes.rs` — `paste_attributes`, cut out of `edit_paste.rs`

  never the array's first) copied onto each target, replaced whole and never
  merged. `PasteGroup` is the five names it takes — the four patch groups and
  `graphic`, which is never in the default set: a graphic's `props` copied
  whole onto clips drawn by the SAME module, the target keeping its name,
  size, `in` and `length`, written with `insert` and `shift_remove`

  action on the target names (`names_prop`) is kept (G-34 (d), amending

  clip lacks and skips a target that cannot take one. **The copied props are

- `edit_zoom.rs` — `add_zoom_action`, the screencast zoom, and `ZoomRegion`,
  the one op ARGUMENT that is a caller-authored object: its `Deserialize` is
  written out rather than derived so it answers as a patch does — an object
  required (a list is not read member by member), an unknown or missing
  member named, a wrong-typed one named by its path. **Its module doc
  IS the placement equation** between the region frame and canvas pixels,
  rotation and crop included; it composes `add_action` + `set_action` +
  `set_action_end` so a drag is one undo step and every refusal is inherited.
- `edit_adjustment.rs` — `Source::Adjustment`'s rules (spec §11 GR-6):
  `add_adjustment_clip`, and the refusals every other door asks it for — a
  transition (from `add_transition`, `set_transition`, `set_transition_style`
  and the overlap rule), a nest, and the blur, sharpen and pixelate filters
  and any blend mode. The recipe draws it as `{"kind":"adjustment"}` (plus its `qualifier` when
  it has one and `selection: true` when `RecipeOptions.selection` names it, GR-13); and on a
  matte track it is dropped before the frame's mattes (inert).
- `edit_background.rs` — `add_background` and `add_blurred_background`: one
  clip on a NEW back-most track, OPS rather than app-side composites because
  the composite carries constraints no half states. A blurred copy drops
  `enabled.audio`, `audio.duck`, the transition, the actions and the label
  (each a wrong picture or a wrong sound if carried) and refuses a nest.
  Default plate colour is white: the canvas is already black.
- `actions.rs` — action evaluation and interpolation, and `clip_state`
  (with a top-level `speed`, `speed_map.rs`'s rate in force, the inspector's
  Rate inside an action, SR-21);
  `video_json` / `color_json` write all thirteen colour keys, the tone keys at
  0 included, for the five callers that must see them (the base state,
  `clip_state`, `patch.rs`'s template, `recipe_layer.rs`, `edit_split.rs`);
  its last line of defence is `actions_clamp.rs`'s, and a graphic's props

  and `clip_state`'s `graphic`. **The LIST rule is stated here once as the
  crate's**: an end patch interpolates a list per index when the lengths
  match and each pair of entries agrees on its discrete fields (`kind`,
  `shape`), and switches at the end otherwise; `video.filters` and `video.obscure` are both governed by it and carry no code of their own.
- `actions_clamp.rs` — `clamp_video`, `clamp_audio` and `clamp_text`, the
  evaluator's last line of defence (`set_action_end` checks a `video`,
  `audio` or `text` end patch's keys and kinds but deliberately not its
  VALUES, and never looks at the clip for them; this bounds every value
  such a patch can carry and forces `normal` on a nest clip), with
  `bounded` / `finite_or`; the first two a pure move out of `actions.rs`

- `actions_curves.rs` — `curves_json` (all six curves, an absent one
  as its domain's identity, for `video_json`'s callers),
  `align_identity_curves` (spec §11 GR-12, GR-32: an identity curve
  meeting a curve of another count in an action takes that curve's x's,
  its ends at 0 and 1 on a tone curve and every value the neutral on a
  hue curve, so a grade animates from neutral), and `CurveBlend`,
  `curve_blends` and `blended_curves_json` (spec §11 GR-34: two

  curve and the eased t in `Evaluated.curve_blends`, and only the recipe
  layer and `clip_state` write it, as `{from, to, t}`; never a file).
- `actions_qualifier.rs` — `qualifier_json` (spec §11 GR-35): a qualifier
  with its `blur` present even at 0, which `actions.rs`'s `video_json` writes
  for a non-neutral one so the blur animates from 0; and `align_hue_center`

  the lerp, an action's target hue centre moves by ±360 when the two
  centres are more than 180° apart, so the centre animates the short
  way round (350 → 10 through 0); `clamp_qualifier` brings it back
  into [0, 360).
- `actions_audio.rs` — the audio group's two evaluation rules (road map
  "audio" AP8b, spec §11 AU-86): `audio_json` writes the group with
  `isolation` present even at 0, which `actions.rs` uses for the base state
  so an action toward an Amount ramps from 0; and `HELD_AUDIO_NUMBERS` (the

  `response`, each response its own curve, AU-66 (f)) with `hold_audio_steps`,
  after the spanning action's `lerp`, holding each at its start value until
  the action's end.
- `actions_color.rs` — `blend_colors` (spec §11 G-43): after the spanning
  action's `lerp`, each of the model's colours — `COLOR_POINTERS`' eight
  `[r, g, b, a]` in `video` and `text` and `CHROMA_KEY_POINTER`'s `[r, g,
  b]`, by path, never by shape — is overwritten by the OKLab blend of the
  action's two ends (`oklab_mix_unit` / `oklab_mix_rgb`), only strictly
  inside the action and only where the ends differ, so an untouched colour
  stays exact; an end of the wrong arity keeps §5.4's hold-then-switch.
- `actions_graphic.rs` — a graphic clip's props at a clip time (format
  version 13, spec §11 G-34): finished actions' `end.graphic.props` laid
  over the clip's map by `insert`, the spanning one interpolated — a number
  in floating point, never rounded; a `color` (by `end.graphic.kinds`,
  never by shape) in OKLab with straight alpha through `model_color.rs`'s
  `oklab_mix` (G-40); anything else, a malformed end, or a prop
  with no start, held and switched at the end. Total. `names_prop` is
  `set_graphic`'s and `paste_attributes`' question.
- `transition.rs` — overlap detection, THE overlap rule (spec §11), eased
  progress at *t*. An overlap with no kind still dissolves
  (`unwrap_or_default`), and `add_clip` onto an overlap mints a
  `cross_dissolve`, so a no-transition baseline is built by moving clips
  apart, not by clearing the kind.
- `transition_search.rs` — the bounded fitting arithmetic for both hard-cut
  transition forms: the old handle decrement path by total, and exact
  forbidden shift intervals across fixed/moved clips for ripple, counted in
  whole grid frames back from the cut (`time::frames_within`). It does
  not enumerate timeline frames; final placements still pass
  `check_overlap_rule`.
- `evaluate.rs` — the A/B assignment, `assign()`, that the plan and the
  recipe share, and `drawing_instances`, which both the instruction tiling
  and the layer list are built from. `assign` leaves a clip's audio out above
  `AUDIO_SPEED_MAX`, and `place` gives every plan audio track ONE `pitch`
  (#190, #211), a `Pitch` (off, spectral, time_domain): keep pitch within
  ×0.999–×1.001 (but not ×1) plays `off`, varispeed, whose pitch change is
  under 1.74 cents (SY-39), and elsewhere within ×0.98–×1.02 `time_domain`
  (SY-26; SY-40 for real speed changes). `Segment`, `CompTrack` and
  `Assignment`'s tracks are `pub(crate)` for `plan.rs` alone. A ramped
  clip (speed ramps SR-10) is placed as ONE unit, its frame-per-segment
  video and its one ramp audio segment (`ramp`, the source map) on the
  same tracks; its ×12 test reads `speed_map.rs`'s `peak_rate` (the greatest
  rate named, not reached, SR-19 (d)) of the instance's own, unlifted clip,
  the same stored numbers Swift's `SpeedAudioDrop.peakSpeed` reads.
- `plan.rs` — `composition_plan()` (spec §7.2): the plan's JSON from
  `assign()`, the instruction tiling, and the decoder-budget warning
  (`MAX_CONCURRENT_VIDEO_TRACKS`). Deterministic to the byte. A pure move
  out of `evaluate.rs` (grading GR1).
- `recipe.rs` · `recipe_layer.rs` · `recipe_options.rs` · `recipe_selection.rs` ·
  `recipe_text.rs` — `frame_recipe(t)`: the layer list at one instant. `RecipeLayer`
  (`recipe_layer.rs`, re-exported by
  `recipe.rs`) is the twenty-six keys of a layer written in ONE place
  (`RecipeLayer.init(from:)` on the Swift side defaults a missing key
  silently, so a copied skeleton drifts with no diagnostic). `RecipeOptions`
  (`recipe_options.rs`, a pure move out of `recipe.rs` in grading-2 G2-0, re-exported by it) is
  what a caller wanted besides `t` — the burn-in timecode, `ungraded` (spec §11 GR-4: every
  layer's `color` written neutral), and `selection` and `behind` (GR-13: `recipe_selection.rs`

  unknown key in silence. A layer whose `transition` or `dissolve` is non-null is

  deliberate overrides of model values (the other: a matte layer's `blend`,
  `shadow` and `reflection`, MT-4), because the dissolve's weight correction
  is the inverse of a fixed-function destination factor, and a routed half
  (`dissolve`) is drawn alone and mixed source-over (spec §11 MT-8). The
  inspector therefore
  shows the model's value while the frame draws `normal` during an overlap.
  `recipe_text.rs` computes what a text layer SHOWS — `Reveal::of` turns
  `text.animation` into `reveal`, `reveal_phase` (the ORDER the renderer draws
  in, not a label on the amount) and `reveal_kind`, folded into the content
