objections.where: How it fits the tree, 'Sizes that set tolls'; SW3/SW4/SW7a 'Depends on'
objections.claim: Tolls the section says CJ0 pays are not in CJ0, and several files SW must grow are at or over the cap with no toll at all.
objections.evidence: SW3 depends on 'CJ0 (... tolls on model.rs, ProjectSnapshot.swift, ReverseRenderer.swift)' and SW4 on 'MediaImporter.swift's named seam (CJ0)'. CJ0's tolls are T1-T10 (cj.md:570-611). Of these files only model.rs (T2) is among them, and cj.md:207 assigns MediaImporter.swift to 'first editor'. Files with no toll: ProjectSnapshot.swift is 1,454 lines, and ClipSnapshot (:1029) takes the stored `audioSource` (SW3) and `link` (SW7a). ReverseRenderer.swift is 574; its named seam is `// MARK: - Settings` at :480. MediaImporter.swift is 589; probeAsset must read every track's channels and title with awaits, which are confined to that file. evaluate.rs is 559 and takes the segment `stream`/`channel`; cj.md:195 says SW pays the Segment→plan_segment.rs toll. ProjectDocument.swift is 1,336; generateCaches at :818 stays there after T7 and takes SW-41's wanted set. edit_time.rs is 595; SW7a's groups change `shifted`, which calls `partner()` at :95 and :120, and cj.md:189 assigns that toll to TX, in another lane. AgentCatalog+Clips.swift is 574 and takes SW7a/SW7b prose. SW7a's Core bullet also omits the other `partner()` callers: edit_edge.rs:73 (slip) and the carried-edge closures at edit_edge.rs:187 and edit_clip_timing.rs:171/:220.
objections.fix: Add an SW toll step at the head of SW3, SW4 and SW7a, each a pure move gated alone, naming its seam. ProjectSnapshot.swift: the `// MARK: - Clips` block 896-1173 → ProjectSnapshot+Clips.swift, which must stay one type (stored properties). ReverseRenderer.swift: `// MARK: - Settings`. MediaImporter.swift: its named thumbnails seam. evaluate.rs: Segment → plan_segment.rs. ProjectDocument.swift: generateCaches into an extension. edit_time.rs: freeze_frame → edit_freeze.rs, or SW7a waits for TX's toll. Correct the 'CJ0' attributions, and list every `partner()` caller in SW7a's Core bullet.

objections.where: Owner's answers applied, 'Lead segments'; the paragraph under the Phases table; Phases table 'Depends on'
objections.claim: Running SW3-SW5 'in a lane of their own' adds a fourth lane, and the table leaves out dependencies the CJ lane plan states.
objections.evidence: The build arrangement allows at most three parallel lanes. cj.md:524-535 assigns lanes A (words), B (recorder) and C (shared, then VR, then SW last), and says 'SW needs CJ3's mouth opening and the clip ceiling'. SW's table names 'CJ Vision lane' instead of CJ3, and omits CJ-9/CJ6 (the clip ceiling SW-24 refuses against) and T8 (the creatorHandlers table that new tools must register in; the section says AgentServer+Switch.swift only). SW4 also rewrites transcript caches (MediaTranscript, DeviceTranscriptCache, Transcriber+Extract) that lane A's TX and FC phases read.
objections.fix: Put the audio-tracks chain in one of the three lanes and record the change as an amendment to CJ-2 (for example, lane C before VR, or lane A after TX's transcript phases, with SW4 after them). Name CJ3, CJ-9/CJ6 and T8 in the Depends-on column.

objections.claim: SW8 specifies its own Vision request and mouth measure, and both conflict with CJ-30's shared `faces` kind.
objections.evidence: CJ-30 (cj.md:409-413) stores mouth opening as 'the inner-lip gap over the face's height', at 10 samples a second and a long side of 1280, with revisions pinned in the kind's version. CJ3's F5 (cj.md:795) says 'over the face's width'. CJ-S2 can drop the rate to 5 a second (cj.md:497) or move mouth opening into its own kind (cj.md:498-499). SW-80 instead fixes revision 3 with the 76-point constellation, and SW-81 divides by 'mouth width', which `faces` does not store. The Vision API exists as claimed (VNRequestFaceLandmarksConstellation, VNFaceLandmarks2D innerLips/outerLips), so the conflict is with CJ-30, not with Apple.
objections.fix: Have SW-80 consume `faces` as CJ-30 stores it: the mouth-opening field and CJ-31's face ids. State SW-81's 0.5 s window in samples at CJ-30's rate, whatever CJ-S2 sets. Any need for a different measure is an amendment to CJ-30, recorded before CJ3's code.

objections.claim: SW's sample table conflicts with CJ's, and SW-S3's ground truth comes from a different recording than the one it runs on.
objections.evidence: CJ (cj.md:909-912) names S-PC1, S-PC2 ('Two people on one microphone, both faces in one shot'), S-MT1 and S-LONG1, kept in tools/proof/media/creator/. SW names S-POD-2CAM, S-POD-SPLIT, S-POD-1MIC ('one microphone between the two people and the two cameras'), S-OBS, S-IPHONE-SPATIAL and S-RECORDER. S-PC2's set-up (one shot holding both faces) contradicts SW8's premise (a camera on each person). SW-S3 'Runs ... on S-POD-1MIC' with 'ground truth from S-POD-2CAM's two-microphone switch', which is a different conversation, and its truth is the algorithm's own output.
objections.fix: Keep one sample table under CJ's names and folder, with S-PC2 matching SW8's premise. For SW-S3, record the one-microphone conversation with the shared microphone and each person's own lavalier running at the same time. Truth is then the lavaliers' unambiguous turns, or the owner's hand-placed markers read back through get_project.

objections.claim: SW-S4's truth on real speech is circular, so the 90 % rule cannot fail on the cases the tuned numbers exist for.
objections.evidence: 'The real excerpt's truth is the steps where one microphone's ℓ − P exceeds the other's by 20 dB'. That is the same loudness-cache feature SW-21 thresholds with `bleed_db` and `dominance_db`. Agreement on those steps is nearly guaranteed, and steps with bleed or crosstalk are left out by construction. 'No shot of a silent listener' is judged against the same circular truth.
objections.fix: Take truth on the excerpt from labelled turns: the owner's markers, or a lavalier per person recorded beside the podcast microphones. Report agreement over all speech seconds, plus false cuts on bleed, and keep SW-S4's rule on that.

objections.where: SW-27, SW2 Acceptance and proof row S1, SW-S4 rule
objections.claim: 'Every cut within one frame of the table' is not achievable on the planner's own grid and is not well defined.
objections.evidence: Activity reads the VAD speech cache on a 32 ms chunk grid and a level averaged over 100 ms, and SW-21 does not say whether that window is centred or trailing. Silero's probability crosses 0.5 one or more chunks after a voice starts, and `say` output starts with variable leading silence. The expected cut (table onset − lead) is therefore off by several 33 ms frames. SW-S4 tunes the defaults to make 'every synthetic case' hit one frame, with no fallback when nothing does.
objections.fix: Define each expected onset from the generated solo voice's measured first sample above a fixed threshold. Set the tolerance from the detection grid (for example one VAD chunk plus half the averaging window plus one frame), and say the averaging window is centred. Pin the two `say` voices and skip by name when they are absent. Give SW-S4 a rule for the case where no setting meets the tolerance.

objections.claim: By default, cameras with their own sound become microphones, which breaks the bet's main workflow.
objections.evidence: 'a microphone is a selected clip that plays sound', and 'a microphone that is itself an angle ... pairs with itself'. In the normal case (cameras with scratch sound plus one microphone file per person, all selected), every camera pairs with itself as a 'lavalier' and the real microphone files have no angles left. The result is a 'speaker without a microphone' refusal or the switch cutting on scratch audio. The survey's pitch is 'a mic per person' (creator-survey.md:315).
objections.fix: By default, a microphone is a selected sound clip whose media has no pictures, which includes a camera's detached sound only when the person picks it in the sheet. A camera's own sound counts as a microphone only when no picture-less sound clip is selected. Add a probe row for that default.

objections.where: SW-20, SW-13, SW-24 ('an angle that does not cover the range')
objections.claim: An angle is a single clip, so a camera whose recording is several files cannot be switched across the file boundary.
objections.evidence: Many cameras split long recordings into several files, and a card change does the same. The three-hour show SW-S2 targets will usually have several clips per camera. SW-24 refuses 'an angle that does not cover the range', and SW-13 lists only clips 'whose span covers the selected clip's whole span'.
objections.fix: Define an angle as a camera's picture clips on one track, or a set the sheet groups. Split each shot range at clip boundaries into one `copy_pieces` per clip. Count a track as covering a span when its clips cover it. Add a two-file angle to F-TURNS.

objections.claim: With an In/Out range set, hiding the angle tracks blanks the timeline outside the range.
objections.evidence: A track is hidden 'when every clip on it in the range is an angle'. `shows_video` reads `track.hidden` for the whole track (nest.rs:140-147), so outside the range the angles disappear while no program shot exists there. The picture falls through to lower tracks or black. The fallback, 'each such angle clip's picture switched off', has the same effect on the clip's parts outside the range.
objections.fix: Hide a track, or switch off a clip's picture, only when the range covers that clip entirely. Otherwise split the angle clips at the range ends and switch off only the inside pieces, or extend the program track with the front angle outside the range. Add an MCP row: `render_frame` outside the range is unchanged by the switch.

objections.where: SW-13, SW-14, SW1 proof row P4
objections.claim: Switch Angle on a shot that has a transition is refused by its own copy step.
objections.evidence: A transition is an overlap of two clips on one track (core/src/transition.rs:1-11). A shot with an incoming or outgoing dissolve shares part of its span with a neighbour. After the shot is deleted, `copy_pieces` 'over the same span' meets SW-11's refusal 'track T holds clip C between A and B'. SW-14 restores only 'its transition' (the incoming one) and does not mention the outgoing overlap, which is the next shot's `transition_in`.
objections.fix: Specify the sequence: record both overlaps, delete the shot, copy over the hard-cut span (the old span less the neighbours' overlaps), then re-add each transition with `add_transition` at its old kind and duration where the handles allow. Name the step 'Switch Angle (transition removed)' when one cannot be re-added. P4 tests a dissolve at each edge.

objections.claim: Leaving undecodable tracks out of `audio_streams` breaks the stream index and SW-30's own promise about stream 0.
objections.evidence: SW-30 says 'A track that does not decode ... is not listed', but also that stream k is AVFoundation's k-th audio track and 'Stream 0 is the track every build has read until now'. Once a track is skipped, entry k no longer names the k-th track that `track(of:mediaType:index:)` looks up. If the undecodable track is the first one (the iPhone Spatial Audio risk), stream 0 is no longer the track builds have read. Audio decodability has no probe today: `DecoderSupport.decodesFirstFrame` runs on the video track only (MediaImporter.swift:103).
objections.fix: Store each entry's AVFoundation `trackID` and look tracks up by ID, or list every track with `decodes: false` and have `set_audio_source` refuse it. State how audio decodability is probed (one buffer through `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput`).

objections.claim: A one-track stereo file carries no channel count, so SW6's main case (a wireless kit's two people on left and right) cannot be checked by the core.
objections.evidence: SW-30 writes `audio_streams` 'only when the file has more than one audio track or a track of more than two channels'. SW-60 allows `channel` 'on any stream of two or more channels'. For a one-track stereo file the core has no record of its channels, and cannot tell it from a mono file. SW-34's relink refusal covers tracks but not a picked channel the new file lacks.
objections.fix: From SW6's format bump, have the probe write the channel count for every media with audio, or at least whenever a channel is picked. Have `set_audio_source` refuse a channel at or past that count. Extend SW-34 to channels.

objections.claim: The core reads speech spans from `media.speech` for ducking, and the section never routes that read through the clip's stream.
objections.evidence: core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs:103 builds a speech ducker's spans from `media.speech`. In SW3 the plan would therefore duck a stream-2 clip at track 0's spans, which contradicts SW-35's 'No reader ever shows track 0's figures for another track'. SW4's Core bullet lists media_speech.rs, op_table.rs and edit_relink.rs, but not audio_duck_speech.rs. Nothing checks `audio_speech` entries or `source.stream` against the media's tracks in `validate` (model_query.rs).
objections.fix: SW3: `speech_spans` gives a clip on a stream other than 0 no spans. SW4: `speech_spans` reads the source's `audio_speech` entry. Add `validate` checks of `source.stream` and `channel` against `audio_streams`, and of each `audio_speech` entry, with core tests.

objections.claim: Per-source cache names miss FC's and CJ5's cache copies, and nothing starts a cache pass after a clip's stream changes.
objections.evidence: FC-21 (fc.md:197-203) copies `thumbs`, `peaks`, `loudness`, `sync`, `speech`, `sound-events` and `device-transcripts` 'by media id', and CJ-51 copies caches into a derived project, so `<id>s<k>` files would be left behind. SW-41 makes a source 'when a clip ... plays it', but generateCaches (ProjectDocument.swift:818) runs at import and open. The only edit-driven pass is the Camera Log observer in `startCaches` (GR-21).
objections.fix: Amend FC-21 and CJ-51 to copy every key of a kept media (`<id>`, `<id>s<k>`, `<id>s<k>c<c>`). Name the trigger: `startCaches`' `.projectDocumentDidChange` observer starts a pass when the wanted set changes. Add a proof row: choose Track 2 in the Source section, then its waveform lands without reopening the project.

objections.claim: SW2, SW3 and SW4 each hold more than one litecode pipeline. Road map 'audio' had to split AP2, AP8 and AP10 after the fact.
objections.evidence: SW3: the core field, op, plan key, relink refusal and format bump; the probe; the builder's track index; the 48 kHz copy key; three offline renderers; the reverse writing every track; SW-35 guards in about nine readers; a new inspector section; 8 proof rows and 6 mutants. SW4: the cache key; four cache passes; the loader; the wanted set and prune; posts and the ledger; eight readers moved; cloud and device transcripts; the core's `audio_speech` with format 39. SW2: the planner, the readings, a new level-series reader, the sheet, the command and the tool, spike SW-S4 inside it, and SW-28's conditional plan change.
objections.fix: Split into SW3a (model, op, play path, Source section, guards) and SW3b (ramp, isolation and voice renders, and the reverse carrying every track). Split SW4a (keys, passes, wanted set, prune, waveform) from SW4b (readers, transcripts, `audio_speech` and its format). Split SW2a (planner, readings, probe, SW-S4) from SW2b (sheet, command, `switch_by_speaker`, MCP proof). objections.where: SW-S1 (a), SW3 proof rows A2 and A3
objections.claim: Nulling Frame Job's export against ffmpeg's decode within −90 dB is not a sound instrument across two AAC decoders or two resamplers.
objections.evidence: SW-S1's fixtures are 'three AAC tracks of distinct tones'; Apple's and ffmpeg's AAC decoders and priming handling differ in the low bits. A3's 44.1 kHz file plays through AudioRateCopy's 48 kHz copy (AudioRateCopy.swift), which uses Apple's resampler, not ffmpeg's. Neither null can reach −90 dB even when the right track plays.
objections.fix: Decide track identity by spectrum: each track's own tone at least 40 dB above the others. Keep the −90 dB nulls for 48 kHz LPCM tracks. For AAC and 44.1 kHz, compare against the same track extracted to its own file (`-map 0:a:k -c copy`) and exported through Frame Job.

objections.where: SW-S2 (c), SW-91, SW9a proof row V1
objections.claim: SW-S2 (c) under-measures the Angle Viewer's load.
objections.evidence: SW-S2 (c) plays 1-4 angles alone. SW-91 adds the angle tracks to the plan beside the program track, whose composition track decodes one of the same files again. The viewer therefore runs N+1 simultaneous 4K decodes plus the compositor's grid pass.
objections.fix: Measure N angles plus a program track that alternates among them, at Half and Full, and state the live-cell rule in terms of that load.

objections.claim: SW-S2 is scheduled in CJ0 without the owner's answer, and its disk and time cost is unplanned.
objections.evidence: Survey decision 8 is unanswered and asked at CJ0 (cj.md:58-60, CJ0 question 4). CJ0's row lists only CJ-S1 and CJ-S2 (cj.md:514). Four two-hour 4K angles at 100 Mb/s are about 90 GB each, and the three-hour file in (d) is about 135 GB; encoding them takes hours. The owner's rules put disk-heavy measurements behind an explicit flag and require asking before any soak over 30 minutes. play_preview plays at most 60 s per call (AgentServer+PlayPreview.swift), so (a)'s five minutes is five calls.
objections.fix: Gate SW-S2 on decision 8, and list SW-S1 and SW-S2 in CJ0's row or move them to SW's first phase. Build (a) and (b) from repeated 10-minute clips of one file. Make only (d) one long file, behind a flag, with its disk and time stated. Say how 60 s calls add up to five minutes.

objections.where: SW-S2 (b), SW9a MCP bullet, SW9b proof row W2
objections.claim: Rows rely on instruments that do not exist and that no phase adds.
objections.evidence: SW-S2 (b) times 'from Playback.update to the item ready', and W2 relies on 'the dev tool counts rebuilds'. No dev tool reports rebuild durations or counts: play_preview answers served frames only (PlaybackTrial.swift). SW9a's `angle_viewer` dev tool answers per-cell frames, not rebuilds.
objections.fix: Name the instrument and the phase that adds it: for example, `play_preview` (or `angle_viewer`) gains a rebuild count and each rebuild's duration from `Playback.startRebuild` to the item being ready, in the dev tools only.

objections.claim: SW9a's FFI is left undecided, and a plan that depends on an option breaks the per-handle plan memo.
objections.evidence: `char *rc_project_composition_plan(const RcProject *p)` takes no options (framejob_core.h:379), so 'the plan's existing options argument, or a new one if there is none' has only one possible answer. `ReelProject.planJSON` is memoised per handle (app/CLAUDE.md, ReelCore.swift's entry), and an export must never include the viewer's hidden tracks. The section also does not say whether View ▸ Angle Viewer persists; proofs may not perform a persisting menu item.
objections.fix: Decide on a new export (for example `rc_project_composition_plan_with(p, options_json)`: Rust, header and ReelCore.swift). Key the memo by the options. State that exports and render_frame never pass the option, that Playback rebuilds on toggle, and that the viewer's shown state is view state, not persisted.

objections.claim: The tap rule checks what the tap sees, but not that a picked channel reaches both sides of the stereo export.
objections.evidence: (b) requires six distinct channels at `prepare`. The tap writes in place on N channels, and the export's mix then folds N channels to two by AVFoundation's rule, which (c) may find unequal. H1 expects 'that channel alone, in both sides'.
objections.fix: Add a round trip to (b): pick channel k, export, and require both sides at k's level within 0.5 dB. Otherwise take the copy branch.

objections.where: Owner's answers applied, 'Lead segments'; the paragraph under the Phases table; Phases table 'Depends on'

objections.claim: SW8 specifies its own Vision request and mouth measure, and both conflict with CJ-30's shared `faces` kind.
objections.evidence: CJ-30 (cj.md:409-413) stores mouth opening as 'the inner-lip gap over the face's height', at 10 samples a second and a long side of 1280, with revisions pinned in the kind's version. CJ3's F5 (cj.md:795) says 'over the face's width'. CJ-S2 can drop the rate to 5 a second (cj.md:497) or move mouth opening into its own kind (cj.md:498-499). SW-80 instead fixes revision 3 with the 76-point constellation, and SW-81 divides by 'mouth width', which `faces` does not store. The Vision API exists as claimed (VNRequestFaceLandmarksConstellation, VNFaceLandmarks2D innerLips/outerLips), so the conflict is with CJ-30, not with Apple.
objections.fix: Have SW-80 consume `faces` as CJ-30 stores it: the mouth-opening field and CJ-31's face ids. State SW-81's 0.5 s window in samples at CJ-30's rate, whatever CJ-S2 sets. Any need for a different measure is an amendment to CJ-30, recorded before CJ3's code.

objections.claim: SW's sample table conflicts with CJ's, and SW-S3's ground truth comes from a different recording than the one it runs on.
objections.evidence: CJ (cj.md:909-912) names S-PC1, S-PC2 ('Two people on one microphone, both faces in one shot'), S-MT1 and S-LONG1, kept in tools/proof/media/creator/. SW names S-POD-2CAM, S-POD-SPLIT, S-POD-1MIC ('one microphone between the two people and the two cameras'), S-OBS, S-IPHONE-SPATIAL and S-RECORDER. S-PC2's set-up (one shot holding both faces) contradicts SW8's premise (a camera on each person). SW-S3 'Runs ... on S-POD-1MIC' with 'ground truth from S-POD-2CAM's two-microphone switch', which is a different conversation, and its truth is the algorithm's own output.
objections.fix: Keep one sample table under CJ's names and folder, with S-PC2 matching SW8's premise. For SW-S3, record the one-microphone conversation with the shared microphone and each person's own lavalier running at the same time. Truth is then the lavaliers' unambiguous turns, or the owner's hand-placed markers read back through get_project.

objections.claim: SW-S4's truth on real speech is circular, so the 90 % rule cannot fail on the cases the tuned numbers exist for.
objections.evidence: 'The real excerpt's truth is the steps where one microphone's ℓ − P exceeds the other's by 20 dB'. That is the same loudness-cache feature SW-21 thresholds with `bleed_db` and `dominance_db`. Agreement on those steps is nearly guaranteed, and steps with bleed or crosstalk are left out by construction. 'No shot of a silent listener' is judged against the same circular truth.
objections.fix: Take truth on the excerpt from labelled turns: the owner's markers, or a lavalier per person recorded beside the podcast microphones. Report agreement over all speech seconds, plus false cuts on bleed, and keep SW-S4's rule on that.

objections.where: SW-27, SW2 Acceptance and proof row S1, SW-S4 rule
objections.claim: 'Every cut within one frame of the table' is not achievable on the planner's own grid and is not well defined.
objections.evidence: Activity reads the VAD speech cache on a 32 ms chunk grid and a level averaged over 100 ms, and SW-21 does not say whether that window is centred or trailing. Silero's probability crosses 0.5 one or more chunks after a voice starts, and `say` output starts with variable leading silence. The expected cut (table onset − lead) is therefore off by several 33 ms frames. SW-S4 tunes the defaults to make 'every synthetic case' hit one frame, with no fallback when nothing does.
objections.fix: Define each expected onset from the generated solo voice's measured first sample above a fixed threshold. Set the tolerance from the detection grid (for example one VAD chunk plus half the averaging window plus one frame), and say the averaging window is centred. Pin the two `say` voices and skip by name when they are absent. Give SW-S4 a rule for the case where no setting meets the tolerance.

objections.claim: By default, cameras with their own sound become microphones, which breaks the bet's main workflow.
objections.evidence: 'a microphone is a selected clip that plays sound', and 'a microphone that is itself an angle ... pairs with itself'. In the normal case (cameras with scratch sound plus one microphone file per person, all selected), every camera pairs with itself as a 'lavalier' and the real microphone files have no angles left. The result is a 'speaker without a microphone' refusal or the switch cutting on scratch audio. The survey's pitch is 'a mic per person' (creator-survey.md:315).
objections.fix: By default, a microphone is a selected sound clip whose media has no pictures, which includes a camera's detached sound only when the person picks it in the sheet. A camera's own sound counts as a microphone only when no picture-less sound clip is selected. Add a probe row for that default.

objections.where: SW-20, SW-13, SW-24 ('an angle that does not cover the range')
objections.claim: An angle is a single clip, so a camera whose recording is several files cannot be switched across the file boundary.
objections.evidence: Many cameras split long recordings into several files, and a card change does the same. The three-hour show SW-S2 targets will usually have several clips per camera. SW-24 refuses 'an angle that does not cover the range', and SW-13 lists only clips 'whose span covers the selected clip's whole span'.
objections.fix: Define an angle as a camera's picture clips on one track, or a set the sheet groups. Split each shot range at clip boundaries into one `copy_pieces` per clip. Count a track as covering a span when its clips cover it. Add a two-file angle to F-TURNS.

objections.claim: With an In/Out range set, hiding the angle tracks blanks the timeline outside the range.
objections.evidence: A track is hidden 'when every clip on it in the range is an angle'. `shows_video` reads `track.hidden` for the whole track (nest.rs:140-147), so outside the range the angles disappear while no program shot exists there. The picture falls through to lower tracks or black. The fallback, 'each such angle clip's picture switched off', has the same effect on the clip's parts outside the range.
objections.fix: Hide a track, or switch off a clip's picture, only when the range covers that clip entirely. Otherwise split the angle clips at the range ends and switch off only the inside pieces, or extend the program track with the front angle outside the range. Add an MCP row: `render_frame` outside the range is unchanged by the switch.

objections.where: SW-13, SW-14, SW1 proof row P4
objections.claim: Switch Angle on a shot that has a transition is refused by its own copy step.
objections.evidence: A transition is an overlap of two clips on one track (core/src/transition.rs:1-11). A shot with an incoming or outgoing dissolve shares part of its span with a neighbour. After the shot is deleted, `copy_pieces` 'over the same span' meets SW-11's refusal 'track T holds clip C between A and B'. SW-14 restores only 'its transition' (the incoming one) and does not mention the outgoing overlap, which is the next shot's `transition_in`.
objections.fix: Specify the sequence: record both overlaps, delete the shot, copy over the hard-cut span (the old span less the neighbours' overlaps), then re-add each transition with `add_transition` at its old kind and duration where the handles allow. Name the step 'Switch Angle (transition removed)' when one cannot be re-added. P4 tests a dissolve at each edge.

objections.claim: Leaving undecodable tracks out of `audio_streams` breaks the stream index and SW-30's own promise about stream 0.
objections.evidence: SW-30 says 'A track that does not decode ... is not listed', but also that stream k is AVFoundation's k-th audio track and 'Stream 0 is the track every build has read until now'. Once a track is skipped, entry k no longer names the k-th track that `track(of:mediaType:index:)` looks up. If the undecodable track is the first one (the iPhone Spatial Audio risk), stream 0 is no longer the track builds have read. Audio decodability has no probe today: `DecoderSupport.decodesFirstFrame` runs on the video track only (MediaImporter.swift:103).
objections.fix: Store each entry's AVFoundation `trackID` and look tracks up by ID, or list every track with `decodes: false` and have `set_audio_source` refuse it. State how audio decodability is probed (one buffer through `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput`).

objections.claim: A one-track stereo file carries no channel count, so SW6's main case (a wireless kit's two people on left and right) cannot be checked by the core.
objections.evidence: SW-30 writes `audio_streams` 'only when the file has more than one audio track or a track of more than two channels'. SW-60 allows `channel` 'on any stream of two or more channels'. For a one-track stereo file the core has no record of its channels, and cannot tell it from a mono file. SW-34's relink refusal covers tracks but not a picked channel the new file lacks.
objections.fix: From SW6's format bump, have the probe write the channel count for every media with audio, or at least whenever a channel is picked. Have `set_audio_source` refuse a channel at or past that count. Extend SW-34 to channels.

objections.claim: The core reads speech spans from `media.speech` for ducking, and the section never routes that read through the clip's stream.
objections.evidence: core/src/audio_duck_speech.rs:103 builds a speech ducker's spans from `media.speech`. In SW3 the plan would therefore duck a stream-2 clip at track 0's spans, which contradicts SW-35's 'No reader ever shows track 0's figures for another track'. SW4's Core bullet lists media_speech.rs, op_table.rs and edit_relink.rs, but not audio_duck_speech.rs. Nothing checks `audio_speech` entries or `source.stream` against the media's tracks in `validate` (model_query.rs).
objections.fix: SW3: `speech_spans` gives a clip on a stream other than 0 no spans. SW4: `speech_spans` reads the source's `audio_speech` entry. Add `validate` checks of `source.stream` and `channel` against `audio_streams`, and of each `audio_speech` entry, with core tests.

objections.claim: Per-source cache names miss FC's and CJ5's cache copies, and nothing starts a cache pass after a clip's stream changes.
objections.evidence: FC-21 (fc.md:197-203) copies `thumbs`, `peaks`, `loudness`, `sync`, `speech`, `sound-events` and `device-transcripts` 'by media id', and CJ-51 copies caches into a derived project, so `<id>s<k>` files would be left behind. objections.fix: Amend FC-21 and CJ-51 to copy every key of a kept media (`<id>`, `<id>s<k>`, `<id>s<k>c<c>`). Name the trigger: `startCaches`' `.projectDocumentDidChange` observer starts a pass when the wanted set changes. Add a proof row: choose Track 2 in the Source section, then its waveform lands without reopening the project.
